details.Use when: You have a lot of heterogeneous content to show on the page, possibly including text blocks, lists, buttons, form controls, or images, and you don’t have room for everything.
details.Problem: User needs to navigate among a website's sections while still being able to quickly browse to the subsection.
details.Solution: Put modules of content into a collinear stack of panels that the user can close and open independently of one another.

details.Use when: Type of information entered can readily be matched with a specific piece of information in the system.
details.Problem: The user needs recognition aided search when performing search tasks that are difficult to remember or easily mistyped.
details.Solution: Suggest possible matches for a search as users are typing.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: Your application or site has a hierarchical structure with two or more levels.
details.Problem: The user needs to know their location in the website's hierarchical structure in order to possibly browse back to a higher level in the hierarchy.
details.Solution: Reveal the user’s hierarchical location and provide links to higher levels.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: Users might perform actions that are difficult or impossible to reverse manually
details.Problem: Cancelability reduces user anxiety and prevent errors by giving users freedom to undo actions
details.Solution: Add a clear Cancel or Stop button near the process or loader. Cancel the action instantly and show a confirmation. For multiple tasks, provide separate buttons to avoid confusion

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: Websites that allow user interactions like comments or registrations are vulnerable to spam bot attacks.
details.Problem: The application needs to verify that the data submitted originates from an actual human and not a robot.
details.Solution: The most popular form of Captchas are images that represent letters, objects or numbers inside.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: You want to provide a high-level overview of key data points in a single information-dense page, updated regularly.
details.Problem: The user wants to digest data from mulitple sources at a glance, need to get a quick update on status, on key information, and on tasks to be done.
details.Solution: It shows useful information, update themselves, usually use graphics to display data.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: You want to show that user has input error, such as a skipped required field or address doesn't exist.
details.Problem: The goal of displaying error messages is to help the user fix their issues and complete their task and recover the poor experience of arriving at a dead link.
details.Solution: Ensure that users know that an error occurred right away, grab users ’ attention to the error.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: The user has questions concerning a site and its related services.
details.Problem: FAQ page is where users are likely to go before going to more detailed help to see if their questions can be answered; many users assume their questions are common and likely asked by others.
details.Solution: Provide a space where users can get answers to common questions. Organize Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) into a separate and routinely maintained section on your site.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: Users need a way to quickly return to specific items within large sets of content.
details.Problem: Favorites help users save and access personally relevant content without searching again.
details.Solution: Let users mark items (e.g., with a star or heart icon) and view them later in a dedicated favorites list.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: Your UI asks the user any questions requiring form-like input (such as text fields), and you want to reduce the amount of work that users need to do.
details.Problem: By providing reasonable default answers to questions, you save the users work.
details.Solution: Pre-fill form fields with a reasonable default value.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: The page contains many content items that have similar style and importance, such as news articles, blog posts, products, or subject areas.
details.Problem: You want to present the viewer with rich opportunities to preview and select these items.
details.Solution: A grid that gives each item equal space announces that they have equal importance.

resources.title: Conferences, Coffee and Complexity: Supporting Cognition and Communication at Conventions

details.Use when: Users enter data and need quick confirmation or correction to prevent errors.
details.Problem: It reduces mistakes, speeds completion, and builds confidence.
details.Solution: Show clear visual or text cues near the field in real time, using accessible colors and concise messages.
